disputed: Lobbying and campaign spending of this kind is legal under current U.S. campaign finance law; whether its scale constitutes undue influence versus ordinary interest-group political participation is a values judgment on which reasonable people disagree, not a legal violation established in this reporting. This entry connects to, but is distinct from, the separate Gaza/genocide-allegation entry in this document.

items: AIPAC made more than $12.7 million in direct PAC contributions to members of Congress and federal candidates in the first half of 2025 alone, and delivered a total of $28 million to congressional campaigns in the 2025-2026 cycle - making it the largest PAC in America this cycle, more than three times the next-largest (the National Association of Realtors). (Sludge (https://readsludge.com/2025/07/25/aipac-gives-millions-in-pac-donations-to-house-allies-senators-in-2026-races/); CB Insights (https://www.cbinsights.com/company/aipac))

Its super PAC, UDP, entered 2026 with a $96 million war chest; the wider pro-Israel donor network entered the 2026 cycle with more than $100 million available. As of August 2026, UDP had spent $54 million on congressional races - the single largest outside spender of the entire midterm cycle per OpenSecrets - with the broader pro-Israel donor network spending $71 million, second only to the cryptocurrency industry. (Tribune/AFP (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2626216/pro-israel-lobby-spends-big-on-us-midterms-as-backlash-grows); CB Insights (https://www.cbinsights.com/company/aipac))

AIPAC has concentrated spending on Democratic primaries specifically to defeat candidates critical of unconditional U.S. military aid to Israel. In 2025, its lobbying (separate from campaign spending, over $1.8 million through Q2 2025) pushed back against a Sen. Bernie Sanders-led effort to block $8.8 billion in weapons sales to Israel on humanitarian grounds, and celebrated the House's rejection of a Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene amendment that would have cut $500 million in Iron Dome funding. (Sludge (https://readsludge.com/2025/07/25/aipac-gives-millions-in-pac-donations-to-house-allies-senators-in-2026-races/))

AIPAC has rejected characterizations that its influence is collapsing amid growing public backlash over U.S.-Israel policy, noting that hundreds of its backed candidates have won primaries, though some of its targeted spending has also produced high-profile losses. (Tribune/AFP (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2626216/pro-israel-lobby-spends-big-on-us-midterms-as-backlash-grows))

summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) is the most prominent pro-Israel lobbying group in U.S. politics. Since 2022, it has shifted from issue-based lobbying to direct campaign spending through its super PAC, the United Democracy Project (UDP).
title: AIPAC lobbying and campaign spending
